Guide

Dressmaker Guide: Sewing Tips and Pattern Advice

Most dresses in Dressmaker are lost before the sewing machine is switched on. Where each pattern piece lands on the cloth, and which way the grain runs through it, is what your customer sees at the end.

Reviewed September 21, 2026

  • Grain firstAlign unless a bias cut is deliberate
  • PrintsKeep large repeats off small panels
  • Before cuttingPreview every layout on the mannequin
  • Seam orderAssemble flat before you close the garment
  • SpendingCheap cloth while you are still learning
  • TrimRescues a plain dress, never a bad cut

Four decisions decide most dresses: match the grain unless a bias cut is deliberate, keep large prints off small panels, preview the layout on the mannequin, and learn on cheap cloth. Trim rescues a plain dress, never a badly cut one.

New to the dressmaker game? Start with how to play Dressmaker.

Quick answers

Every tip here, in one line.

QuestionShort answer
Align to the grain or cut on the bias?Align by default
When is a bias cut worth it?Simple shape, fluid cloth
Big print on a small panel?Move it to a bigger piece
One fabric for the whole dress?One drape per dress
What order do I sew in?Flat first, sleeves before hems
The dress looks wrong?Run the fix list below

Grain and bias

Lengthwise grain runs parallel to the selvedge and stretches least. Align to it by default.

CutWhat it doesUse it when
On grainHangs square, keeps its seamsBodices, waistbands, straight skirts
On the biasStretches, ripples, drapesFluid cloth, no stripes or plaid

The official Steam description says your arrangement and your cut are what show on the final dress.

Warning

bias beside straight grain behaves like a different cloth at the seam.

Print scale vs pattern piece size

If the repeat is wider than the piece, that piece captures a fragment — one petal, half a stem.

  • Stripes must meet at the seam. A band that steps up by a fraction is obvious.
  • Plaid matches two ways, so place pieces to suit the repeat.
  • Mirrored pieces make a chevron. Good at a center back seam, a mistake at a side.

Tip

give a panel one full repeat, and save the big floral for the skirt.

Fabric, panel by panel

A crisp bodice over a fluid skirt is a choice; mixed drape is an accident.

FabricBehaves likeBest forWatch out for
CottonHolds a line, easy to handleEveryday dresses, bodicesFlat on a full skirt
LinenCrisp, visible weaveSummer dressesFights a busy print
WoolDense, hangs heavyTailored winter skirtsRigid under a soft shape
SilkFluid, holds nothingBias cuts, soft skirtsShows every pucker
VelvetDeep color, adds weightStatement dressesReverse cuts read as two colors

Note

in-game fabric stats are not published. The mannequin is your measurement.

Layout before you cut

Nothing later repairs a bad layout, so plan the whole table first.

  1. 1

    Tile the big pieces first

    skirt, back and sleeves.

  2. 2

    Fit small pieces into gaps

    what the big pieces leave.

  3. 3

    Decide what you optimize for

    minimum waste and a matched repeat differ.

  4. 4

    Keep direction consistent

    prints and naps face one way.

  5. 5

    Stay off the selvedge

    it prints a different shade.

  6. 6

    Keep every offcut

    the cheapest practice cloth you will get.

Tip

preview every layout on the mannequin. It is the last free check.

Warning

cutting is permanent. The fabric is spent when the shears go through it.

Seam order

Sew in an order that keeps the fiddly work flat.

  1. 1

    Build small pieces into big ones

    while everything is flat.

  2. 2

    Close the shoulders and side seams

    two panels become a tube.

  3. 3

    Set the sleeves while the body is open

    easier than a finished dress.

  4. 4

    Finish hems and openings last

    the edges you handle most.

Tip

place buttons, bows and appliqué flat on the table. The machine's bobbin never runs out.

Decoration discipline

Trim frames a good cut or points at a bad one. It never hides a broken print.

  • One focal point per dress

    Busy fabric wants quiet trim; plain fabric carries a statement.

  • Match the trim to the occasion

    Lace and heavy appliqué for formal work; everyday dresses want restraint.

  • Clutter is the easiest mistake

    Three trims fighting for attention read as noise.

The full game has over 350 accessories, so restraint is worth learning.

Read the customer before you sew

Designing before you know the occasion, the taste and the numbers wastes a bolt.

  1. 1

    Read the occasion

    a wedding and a market stall differ.

  2. 2

    Read the taste

    what this client likes, in her own words.

  3. 3

    Read the numbers

    the sketchbook lists attribute targets; one screenshot reads Quality 70, Flowers 60, Cute 30, Romantic 45.

  4. 4

    Design in the sketchbook

    from what your shop stocks.

Hand-in pays coin and reputation; the customer card shows a star rating.

Note

how the stars are calculated has never been published.

See Dressmaker customer preferences for reading a brief, and missing on purpose.

Coin, reputation and which bolt to spend

Cloth you buyWhat it buys you
Cheap cottonPractice at layout and seam order
An expensive bolt for a paying commissionA dress the customer remembers
A dress sold off the rackSteady coin, nobody's wedding on it

Coin buys the next bolt; reputation is what the town remembers.

Tip

while you are learning, buy the cheapest cloth that fits the brief.

Note

fabric prices, coin amounts and reputation thresholds are not published.

Fix a dress that looks wrong

Check these before you blame the sewing.

What you seeLikely causeWhat to do
Silhouette sags or stands awayCloth fighting the shapeChange the bolt, not the pattern
Print looks brokenRepeat bigger than the panelCut it from a bigger piece
Stripes step at a seamLayout faultNothing fixes it after cutting
One panel a different colorNap, on velvetCut every panel the same way
The hem wavesBias beside straight grainRe-cut, or even it out
It looks fussyToo much trimTake one trim off
The dress is fine, the customer is notYou missed the occasionRe-read the brief; customer preferences covers it

Dressmaker rewards workroom habits: plan the cut, respect the grain, spend cloth where it shows. The Dressmaker wiki holds the reference tables, the dressmaker game homepage covers the release and the free prototype, and games like Dressmaker is next.
